subject: design/merge-lane-v1
statement: The **risk policy** is one dedicated file at the repo's config surface (the system config carries only its path key): closed schema, own schema version, floor classes, the AUTO-eligible class set — each class a data-defined predicate (name, whole-diff path perimeter, precondition flags) per §3.1 — thresholds, the activation block, and the kill switch field. A **shared validator verb** enforces the closed parse everywhere the policy is read, refuses any policy — however well-formed — whose floor fails to cover §3.1's self-unlock minimum **or whose AUTO code class claims the lane's build inputs (`go.mod`/`go.sum`) in its perimeter** (§3.1's trust-base rule; a class perimeter and the self-unlock minimum may not overlap on those paths), and detects "unratified" at load: the policy is read from its mainline lineage, where every change landed only through the ratification check, and content whose fingerprint does not match that trailer-ratified lineage refuses to load (DINV-8, DINV-9). Every change lands only with the operator's recorded ratification — the existing gate-policy trailer mechanism widened to the policy home (AP-24 made mechanical); **that widening is this design's one sanctioned check delta**: additive coverage over a path class that exists only with this feature, so every pre-existing tree's verdict stays byte-identical — NR-1's real bar, verified at A-9 — carved out explicitly from §3.2's no-check-change line. The **lane verdict record** rides the proposal as a structured, versioned block per evaluation (append-only across evaluations); the **act** self-describes in the medium's durable history — the approval and merge carry the machine identity, the head revision, the policy version, and the consumed reviewer-verdict ref where the class carries one. **The reviewer-verdict read (DINV-3's precondition), defined**: where an AUTO class carries it, the verdict enters as a **required check context** — a registered mechanical arm validates the artifact class's review report (structural validity against its template, an approving verdict, the report's recorded subject fingerprint matching the evaluated content, and authoring commits carrying the reviewer-flow attribution the shipped attribution arms enforce) and publishes a check state the lane consumes through the already-pinned check-state snapshot — never by parsing the proposal's own content, which is exactly where a planted verdict is told apart from a produced one (A-7's red fixture). **This arm is part of the lane's trust base**: its code home is in the lane's own packages inside the self-unlock minimum (§3.1), so an edit to it floor-hits HUMAN under the mainline policy, and — like the classifier — it runs from the trusted mainline context (DINV-9), never built or executed from the evaluated proposal's tree, so neither an arm-code edit nor a build-input substitution riding a code class can corrupt the source DINV-3 trusts. The **lane-state record** is the fourth data class — the halted state's home: a repo-resident datum on a dedicated lane-state ref outside the protected branch namespace, written **synchronously by the acting workflow step at goal-verify failure, before any further act**, read together with the policy's kill and activation fields at every act gate and state read — so lane state (NFR-5) resolves from the repo alone. The record's **write/clear authority is enforced by a named mechanism, not merely asserted** — the property matters precisely because branch protection does not guard a ref outside the protected namespace, so any repo-write actor could otherwise forge a clear or delete the ref to un-halt the I2-class circuit breaker: **(1)** a **platform ref-protection** restricts the lane-state namespace to the machine identity — an activation-time operator precondition listed beside the org-backstop act (§3.7), read as data, never performed or scheduled by this design (FR-9's pattern); **(2)** the **act gate validates before honoring a cleared state** — it accepts a "cleared" reading only when the record's writer is the machine identity and each clear entry cites a **human disposition recorded on the affected drive's delivery ledger** (the named recording surface — the argus alarm surface), refusing a non-machine write or an uncited clear (a forged clear or ref deletion is refused; a planted halt is fail-safe — it only over-stops). A recorded human disposition — a delivery-ledger entry the clear cites — is the only clearer. The **shadow agreement report** is a committed artifact computed from the records alone. Field-level schemas, the verdict-record block format, the act self-description template, and the state-resolution rule are the paired solution-shape's content (`shape:merge-lane-v1`), authoritative until the implementing code lands.
